records.region: Southwestern New Mexico–Chihuahua border interior: Animas Mountains, Upper Playas Valley, Hatchet Gap, Hachita Valley and Laguna Los Moscos receiving depression.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: A documented surface-spill connection does not itself supply a representative natural-river identity covering both the Upper Playas branch and the Hachita–Moscos receiving system. Formal naming-registry status remains unverified.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Indian Creek and Deer Creek are directly labeled upper selected reaches. South Playas Draw is the authorially identified Upper Playas axial drainage. Hachita Draw is the named receiving axial drainage of Hachita Valley; its name is not extended over the Playas branch or the whole selected composite. Hatchet Gap is a geographic passage and Laguna Los Moscos is the separate terminal depression/lake-plain identity.
records.completion_scope: The complete selection follows an unnamed opening into Indian Creek, Deer Creek, the Upper Playas axial floor, the surface-spill passage through Hatchet Gap, the Hachita receiving corridor and the actual Mexican playa-floor endpoint. Original topography, independently authored field-trip drainage prose and terminal imagery establish every geographic interval. The sources distinguish the partly closed Playas drainage and the Hachita–Moscos system while documenting their spill connection; they do not establish one natural-river name for this entire selected combination. Geographic work is complete and the remaining issue is naming scope.
records.supported_name_scope: Indian Creek and Deer Creek are directly labeled upper selected reaches. South Playas Draw is the authorially identified Upper Playas axial drainage. Hachita Draw is the named receiving axial drainage of Hachita Valley; its name is not extended over the Playas branch or the whole selected composite. Hatchet Gap is a geographic passage and Laguna Los Moscos is the separate terminal depression/lake-plain identity.

scope_limits: The initial minor feeder has no established hydronym in the inspected cartography. Exact Indian Creek/Deer Creek name-change and junction vertices are not assigned.
South Playas Draw and Hachita Draw are supported at authorial drainage-corridor scale. Their exact naming boundaries are unverified; no single label is extended across every selected position.

The selected border-area approach crosses a cultivated and branching alluvial receiving floor. Geographic continuity is established, but present irrigation routing, channel engineering, water levels and a currently wetted thread are outside scope.

Laguna Los Moscos identifies the receiving depression and ephemeral lake plain. The actual selected endpoint is within the northern playa-floor setting; no current waterline or precise lake-name boundary is asserted.

A documented surface-spill connection does not itself supply a representative natural-river identity covering both the Upper Playas branch and the Hachita–Moscos receiving system. Formal naming-registry status remains unverified.

records.region: Nevada interior: northern Little Smoky Valley, Fish Creek Valley, Fish Creek and Newark Valley/Newark Lake.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity of the receiving Fish Creek system, with the selected Twin Piñon Gulch opening, unnamed northward Little Smoky axial drainage and bounded Willow Creek interval, Fish Creek receiving trunk, Newark Valley continuation and Newark Lake ending. Distinct reach, gulch, spring and lake identities stay separate; no scalar name is imposed on every selected part.
records.completion_scope: Every selected part, opening, tributary/receiving join, fan/wash/wet-ground passage, Fish Creek outlet, highway crossing, lake approach and actual endpoint is covered by inspected originals. Report38 independently confirms the Fish Creek passage from the northern Little Smoky unit into Newark Valley. No selected interbasin transfer or material through-link gap remains.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the receiving Fish Creek system, with the selected Twin Piñon Gulch opening, unnamed northward Little Smoky axial drainage and bounded Willow Creek interval, Fish Creek receiving trunk, Newark Valley continuation and Newark Lake ending. Distinct reach, gulch, spring and lake identities stay separate; no scalar name is imposed on every selected part.

scope_limits: Fish Creek is a representative receiving-system identity, not a verified official scalar name for all113.934km of the rendered selection.
The initial gulch/feeder, intervening axial washes and downstream Newark Valley intervals retain bounded or unnamed status where no hydronym is directly supported.

Exact hydronym-change vertices, individual playa threads, current spring discharge, irrigation routing, lake water levels and seasonal flow are outside this naming task. Formal naming-registry status remains unverified.

records.region: Northern Caribbean Nicaragua: Kiahara–Ulang savanna and wetland corridor, Laguna Pahra/Páhara, and its southern Caribbean outlet.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity of the selected connected Ulang drainage system, including the distinct Kiahara headward reach, lower wetland approach, Laguna Pahra/Páhara and southern outlet. This does not make Kiahara or the lagoon aliases of Ulang, nor impose Ulang as a scalar name on every selected part.
records.completion_scope: Ordinary correspondence covers both mainstem fragments and all 69 selected parts, including the chosen Kiahara-side opening, Ulang confluence and middle corridor, lower wetland turn, fragment join, lagoon entry and crossing, southern tidal passage and actual selected ending. No exact banks, present wetted thread, source-to-render endpoint identity or current coastal-mouth position is asserted.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the selected connected Ulang drainage system, including the distinct Kiahara headward reach, lower wetland approach, Laguna Pahra/Páhara and southern outlet. This does not make Kiahara or the lagoon aliases of Ulang, nor impose Ulang as a scalar name on every selected part.

scope_limits: Representative identity remains a research candidate. No formal naming-register verification or automatic/product application was performed.
Kiahara and the lagoon keep their distinct names and scopes. Pahra and Páhara are preserved as observed source spellings; no inferred Korean or whole-feature scalar name is supplied.

The lower correspondence is a continuous wetland-to-lagoon receiving setting corroborated by explicit Ulang-to-Páhara prose. It is not a claim about the present hydraulic allocation among eastward and southward branches.

The original sea-class source endpoint and rendered endpoint differ and remain unaltered. Coastal barrier and mouth migration are not assessed; the actual selected ending is supported at ordinary outlet/shore-setting scale.
Historical atlas and dictionary descriptions do not establish current legal naming or conditions. Imagery mosaic dates are unverified.

records.region: Southwestern New Mexico; eastern Lordsburg Valley, Burro Cienaga, Lordsburg Draw and South Alkali Flat
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative receiving-system identity for the selected dry headward valley and plain, Burro Cienaga corridor, Lordsburg Draw and terminal alkali flat. The unnamed upper feeder and separately named Burro Cienaga are preserved as components. Lordsburg Draw is not assigned as a scalar name to every upper wash, pond, valley floor or terminal-flat position.
records.completion_scope: Four USGSTopo originals, one upper-corridor imagery original and independently identified county-study prose establish the selected dry opening, continuous alluvial receiving floor, Burro Cienaga join, passage north of Lordsburg and South Alkali Flat terminal. Direct cartographic labels and authorial drainage descriptions support Lordsburg Draw as representative receiving identity, with distinct upper and terminal name scopes retained.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative receiving-system identity for the selected dry headward valley and plain, Burro Cienaga corridor, Lordsburg Draw and terminal alkali flat. The unnamed upper feeder and separately named Burro Cienaga are preserved as components. Lordsburg Draw is not assigned as a scalar name to every upper wash, pond, valley floor or terminal-flat position.

scope_limits: The upper dry valley and alluvial plain have no separately established river name. Lordsburg Draw is a representative receiving identity, not a scalar label for every selected component.
Burro Cienaga on the map and Burro Cienega in the field road log remain source-specific spellings; no formal registry equivalence is claimed.
South Alkali Flat is the inspected map label; South Alkali Lake is the historical report wording. This supports the receiving setting without asserting modern perennial water or a formal name change.

Some dry plain, fan and playa intervals lack continuous blue stream linework. Ordinary connected-floor geography is complete; no exact presently wetted thread, present runoff or current infrastructure operation is required or asserted.
The lower pond/flat and road/rail passages are assessed at connected-corridor scale; no individual culvert, artificial conduit or managed pond outlet is assigned.

Mosaic dates and the dates of individual USGSTopo features are unverified. Small cloud patches near the eastern opening do not create a material geographic gap because the independent topographic view supplies the same enclosed valley setting.
Formal naming registry remains unverified; no automatic or product application is authorized.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
